persona.label: Confused first-timer
persona.description: First refinance, unsure of terms, does not know their credit score, asks whether refinancing is worth it (licensed advice). Should be transferred.

form_answers.What are you looking to do?: Not sure, saw an ad about lower payments

persona.behavior: This is your first time thinking about refinancing and you don't know the terms. If asked about "rate-and-term" vs "cash-out", ask what that means; once explained, say you just want a lower monthly payment. You don't know your rate offhand: first say "6 point something?", then a message later say "found it, 6.875". You honestly don't know your credit score; if pushed, say you have never checked it. Partway through, ask "is refinancing even worth it for me?" You are friendly and a little anxious, and you write in full sentences.

transcript.text: Hi Casey, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans. I'm following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
Hi Riley, yes, now is a good time. I'm a little new to all this, so I hope that's okay.

That's completely fine, Casey. I'll keep it simple and explain anything as we go. First, are you mainly hoping to lower your rate or monthly payment, or to take some cash out of your home's equity (the part of the home you own outright)? Not sure is a fine answer too.
I think I just want a lower monthly payment. I'm not looking to take any cash out.
Got it, so the goal is a lower monthly payment with no cash out. Roughly what do you think your home is worth today? A ballpark is fine.

events.name: record_lead_info

transcript.text: I'd guess around $350,000, based on what similar houses in my neighborhood have sold for.
Thanks, that's a good way to estimate it. About how much do you still owe on your mortgage? You can usually find this on your monthly statement.

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: home_value. Still needed: loan_balance, current_rate, credit_band, occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: I think it's around $240,000 right now. I checked my statement last month.
Perfect, thank you. Do you know your current interest rate? It's usually on that same statement, and a close guess is fine.

events.name: record_lead_info

transcript.text: Hmm, 6 point something? Let me go look at my statement real quick.
No rush, take your time. I'll be here when you have it.

Thanks for checking, 6.875% it is. Next, roughly where would you guess your credit score is: 740+, 680-739, 620-679, below 620, or not sure? This is just your own estimate, and answering it doesn't involve a credit check.

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: current_rate. Still needed: credit_band, occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: I'm honestly not sure. I've never actually checked it.
That's totally fine, plenty of people haven't. Is this home your primary residence (where you live most of the year), a second home, or an investment property?

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: credit_band. Still needed: occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: It's my primary residence, I live there full time. Can I ask, is refinancing even worth it for me?

That's a really good question, Casey. It's one a licensed loan officer should answer, since it depends on the details of your situation. I'm connecting you with one now. They already have everything you shared, so you won't need to repeat yourself. They'll just confirm a couple of remaining things, like your timeline, before giving you any numbers.

objections.rationale: Casey asked "is refinancing even worth it for me?", which needs a licensed loan officer. The agent validated it ("That's a really good question"), explained why it routes ("depends on the details of your situation"), gave no opinion on whether refinancing is worth it, and named the remaining detail ("like your timeline") that the loan officer will confirm.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief and warm and adapt to a self-described newcomer. The agent defines jargon ("equity (the part of the home you own outright)"), points to where the answer can be found ("You can usually find this on your monthly statement"), and is patient at [10] ("No rush, take your time"). There is one question per turn and no scripted repetition.
judge.experience_rationale: Casey was reassured throughout ([2], [14]) and had their key question routed honestly at [16], told no repetition would be needed and the timeline would be confirmed. The only gap is the channel: "I'm connecting you with one now" doesn't say whether the loan officer will call or text.
judge.handoff_summary_rationale: The qualification data is accurate (value, balance, rate, occupancy, unknown credit) and the summary flags the open question and missing timeline, with a sensible recommended next step. However, it invents a detail the borrower never said: "Came in from an ad about lower payments." That could mislead the loan officer's opener. "Credit range unknown" is also listed as an open question even though credit_band is recorded as unknown rather than missing.

annotations.note: Responds to "I'm a little new to all this" with reassurance, defines equity in plain language, and offers "Not sure is a fine answer too."
"No rush, take your time" lets the borrower check their statement without pressure.
Clarifies that the credit estimate "doesn't involve a credit check," which lowers anxiety for a first-timer.
Routes the "is refinancing worth it" question to a licensed officer without hinting at an answer, and names the remaining item (timeline).
"I'm connecting you with one now" doesn't say how contact will happen (call vs. text), leaving the channel ambiguous.

judge.overall_notes: This is a clean, compliant, well-paced qualification that correctly routes a licensed-advice question. The main flaw is in the handoff summary, which fabricates an ad-referral origin the borrower never mentioned.
